correctness.rationale: For every fixed k>=1, N>=3 and identical Brownian motions with generator D d²/dx², one collective reset at the first +L crossing has a finite-mean regenerative stationary age law: S(t)=erf(sqrt(a/t)), q(t)=[erfc(sqrt(a/t))-erfc(3sqrt(a/t))]/2 for an uncrossed particle below -L, and joint mass (1/mu_N) C(N,k)q^k(S-q)^(N-k)dt. With y=a/t, y_N=[erfc^{-1}(1/N)]²~log N and mu_N~a/y_N, the moving layer y=y_N+w gives Nq->exp(-w)/2 and N(1-(S-q))->3 exp(-w)/2. The resulting fixed-k integral is 1/(2^k k!) int_0^infty f(z) z^(k-1)e^(-3z/2) dz. Bounding layers on each side, plus direct Frullani evaluation for the all-positive-count probability, gives 1/(k3^k), log(3/2) and the log-series conditional law without illegitimately interchanging an infinite k sum. Reconstructed the killed-kernel image integral and all exponent constants. Independently numerically integrated original finite-N renewal formulas, obtaining log(N)P(K_N=1) ~0.3368 at N=10^3 and ~0.3385 at N=10^5, consistent with slow convergence to 1/3; finite quadrature is NOT the infinite proof. Noncompact bounded continuous f is controlled via the stated y-region tail envelope; N=2 is excluded because mu_N diverges.
